claims.text: CoCrFeMnNi HEA can be deposited on and adhered to a Cu matrix surface.
Modifying the surface chemistry of the Cu matrix enhances interfacial bonding with CoCrFeMnNi HEA.
CoCrFeMnNi HEA exhibits excellent wear resistance because of its high entropy and unique microstructure.
The initial Cu surface is clean and roughened.
A 1–5 μm CoCrFeMnNi layer is deposited on Cu by sputtering or electroplating at 1–10 nm/s.
Deposition is conducted at 10^-5 mbar and a substrate temperature of 200–300°C.
Deposition forms a 10–50 nm interfacial layer between Cu and the HEA.
The interfacial layer consists of Cu–HEA intermetallic compounds and/or a compositional gradient.
Diffusion and mechanical mixing during deposition facilitate formation of the interfacial layer.
The interfacial layer enhances Cu–HEA adhesion through mechanical interlocking, chemical bonding, and diffusion.
The CoCrFeMnNi HEA has a mixture of FCC and BCC phases.
High entropy and mixed FCC/BCC microstructure contribute to the HEA's wear resistance and adhesion.
The coating increases adhesion strength by 20–50% relative to a baseline value of 10 MPa.
The predicted adhesion increase is caused by enhanced interfacial bonding and the HEA microstructure.
Changes in substrate temperature or deposition rate can affect interfacial-layer formation and adhesion.
The long-term stability and corrosion or degradation resistance of the HEA layer are not well understood.

contradictions.description: Electroplating is presented as an alternative deposition technique, but the universal condition of deposition in a 10^-5 mbar vacuum chamber is incompatible with conventional liquid-electrolyte electroplating.

The predicted outcome compares Cu–HEA interfacial adhesion with a 10 MPa baseline, while the stated baseline is bare, uncoated Cu and therefore has no Cu–HEA interface whose adhesion strength could be measured.
